title: protect.js poll cadence in getSleepLength trades merge-gate latency against GitHub API quota
answers: How often does protect.js poll checks while waiting for CI?
Why does the Protect workflow fail early or use a 15 second retry?
Changing the protect workflow polling interval and rate limit impact
body:
Invariant: getSleepLength(iterationCount, numPendingJobs) is the only place that sets the wait between Protect sweeps. Its first two post-sweep sleeps are 15s regardless of pending job count, then 30s (<=7 pending) or 5 min.
Enforced by: .github/workflows/protect.js:getSleepLength.
What breaks if skipped: each sweep runs fetchChecks, which can make several paginated GitHub API calls (workflow runs and jobs per run). Shortening early intervals raises API pressure on busy PRs and makes rate-limit exhaustion more likely; lengthening them delays failure detection on an already-completed check.
Constraints: the 15s early cadence is intended to surface early failures before the 30s/5min backoff. Review flagged rate-limit risk for this tradeoff; any further change to early intervals should be weighed against that cost.
applies: Applies to poll timing in .github/workflows/protect.js only; not to other workflow scripts.
says: The pull request protection workflow hits API rate limits during busy development periods.
Branch protection checks take several minutes to notice when pending builds have completed.
Speed up how frequently the merge gate checks for completed or failed test suites.
Why does the pull request status take five minutes to refresh between checks?
Detect early build failures faster without exhausting our platform request quota on pull requests.
